They retain their own social and commercial identities and there is no justification for regarding them as single communities for the purpose of defining their commercial zones. Today, many metropolitan areas are comprised of two or more separately incorporated municipalities. Application of the twin city concept to all of these metropolitan areas would commence an endless process or reevaluating the commercial zone of every city which is in the vicinity of another city. Such a process would be administratively undesirable and contrary to the intent of this proceeding to simplify the regulations pertaining to commercial zones.
